newsitem.title: UK: Libya sentences eight to death as spies.
newsitem.headline: Libya sentences eight to death as spies.

text.p: Libya's top military court has sentenced six senior officers and two civilians to death for spying, Libyan television reported on Wednesday.
It said they were convicted on passing defence secrets to foreign governments and belonging to "a banned organisation linked to agents of foreign governments".
Six other officers and two civilians were acquitted, said the report monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Six of those sentenced would be executed by firing squad and two by hanging, it said.

"The Supreme Military Court ... has passed its sentences against the agent-spies who sold their honour, dignity and homeland to their enemies and supplied agents of foreign governments with information relating to the country's defence secrets, for espionage purposes, by exploiting their membership of the Libyan army," Libyan television said.

"With these sentences, those who broke the oath and offered themselves as tools to the enemies of the revolution and the people ... receive the punishment they deserve for the disgrace they brought on the homeland and the shame they caused to the nation and revolution."
